question: What does the Autel EVO Max 4N do when the control link is lost, and do incident reports match?

intake.focus: Autel EVO Max 4N control link loss behavior
intake.reason: User asks what happens when control link is lost and whether NASA ASRS incident reports align with that behavior, per approved references (Autel manual, FAA AC 107-2A, NASA ASRS).

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance says to reestablish the control link and, if not possible, start emergency or contingency procedures; Appendix A notes loss of control scenarios and the need to describe actions in the preflight briefing. Autel EVO Max 4N manuals state that on C2 link loss during automated missions, a preset Signal Loss Action is executed after 10 seconds, with options including Return to Home, Hover, or Land, plus voice alerts. Incident reports (unverified) claim loss of control shortly after takeoff with attempted Return To Home failures. Main gap: conflict between FAA guidance and the incident report, plus missing evidence on reestablishment, which Signal Loss Action was configured, whether voice alerts worked, and whether a loss preflight was reviewed.

gaps.text: Conflict: Incident report claims loss of control with RTH failure; Autel manual states Signal Loss Action is executed after loss and may include RTH.
Conflict: FAA guidance requires reestablishing control link or contingency procedures; incident report does not address reestablishment.
Missing: No verified evidence of Autel voice alerts on C2 link loss in the incident.
Missing: No corroboration of the 10-second threshold triggering Signal Loss Action in the incident.
Missing: Which Signal Loss Action option (Return, Hover, Land) was configured for this flight.
Unclear: Whether preflight briefing for loss-of-control procedures was included in this operation.
